title: Headless Claude Code with DD hooks: where the task report is, and how the runner handles a flaky suite
body: In a headless run with DD's hooks (`claude -p ... --output-format stream-json --verbose --include-hook-events`), the agent's task report is the assistant text after its last tool call and before the Stop hook_response that adds context; the result event's text is the reply to DD's Stop capture request ("I'm not proposing a memory from this turn"). A blind judge handed that text penalises DD and learns the condition (seen 2026-10-07); taskReport in src/eval/agent/metrics.js cuts at the right place. Register the hooks from hooks/hooks.json, never by hand. The suite in a fresh clone can still flake under load: src/eval/bench/run.js reruns it through src/eval/bench/suite.js and records both outcomes (suite_first_passed, suite_flaky) rather than counting a flake against the agent. The telemetry lock test (`a write waits for another process holding the telemetry lock instead of failing`) failed first in 5 of 80 runs of the 2026-10-14 trial; on 2026-10-20 its lock holder gained `PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000`, as openTelemetry sets, which removed the race Windows CI also hit. A flake of it after that date is new.
not_derivable: metrics.js implements the cut; why it is needed (the judge reading DD's Stop reply) and the lock test's flaky history live only in the trial write-ups kept out of git.

evidence.summary: taskReport stops at a Stop hook_response that adds context.
Records suite_first_passed and suite_flaky for each run.
The lock holder sets PRAGMA busy_timeout = 5000 (2026-10-20).
